subject: Chain of trust: request for subprocessor roster + provenance artifacts
messages:
From: Aimee Harris <aimee.harris@medicore.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: subprocessor roster + provenance artifacts for SIG review

Hi Michael —

Hope you’re well. We’ve started the SIG Lite review for the integration project (MED-4852) and our GRC team needs the following to progress the control mappings:

- A complete list of current subprocessors (names, roles, locations, and data access scope).
- Proof of provenance for any third-party inference runtime or KV cache providers (attestations, residency statements, or CAIQ references).
- Any onshore/offs shore residency restrictions or escrow plans you have for critical dependencies.

If you can share a CSV roster and a short bundle of artifacts (PDFs preferred), we can close the open SIG questions. Our timeline is tight — ideally by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks,
Aimee
Aimee Harris
Senior Security Programs Manager
Medicore

[attachment: request-checklist.pdf (stub)]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Aimee Harris <aimee.harris@medicore.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: subprocessor roster + provenance artifacts for SIG review

Hi Aimee —

Thanks for the clear ask. I’m attaching a roster extract and a provenance addendum that should address most of the SIG Lite questions. Short notes:

- Attached CSV (redwood_subprocessors_20250903.csv) contains: vendor, service, location(s), data scope, contact, and whether they handle PKI/KMS.
- Provenance addendum (sig-lite_provenance_addendum.pdf) includes statements from our inference runtime partner about residency and a CAIQ reference link for our KV cache provider.
- Onshore-only dependencies are flagged in the CSV (column: residency_restriction).

Irene — can you please confirm the KV cache residency language and attach the runtime partner attestation if available? Ben — can you note any contracts with escrow/residency clauses that Medicore should be aware of?

Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood_subprocessors_20250903.csv (stub), sig-lite_provenance_addendum.pdf (stub)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Aimee Harris <aimee.harris@medicore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: subprocessor roster + provenance artifacts for SIG review

Hi all —

Following up with the clarifications Michael asked for. A few specifics to call out from the provenance addendum:

- KV cache provider (CacheWave) — CAIQ ID: CAIQ-CacheWave-2025-05. CacheWave has an EU and US region; our account is provisioned in US-west by default. We have a written residency statement from them (excerpt included in the PDF).
- Inference runtime partner (TorchServeX) — they provided a notarized runtime attestation confirming no downstream subprocessors have access to customer plaintext prompts; only encrypted telemetry is forwarded. I’ve attached the attestation snippet.
- Escrow/residency: for on-prem kits we use a certified third party (CustodyVault) under SSO-bound escrow; details are in Appendix B of the addendum.

Ben — Ben confirmed via contract review that there is a limited escrow clause with CustodyVault for customers requiring air-gapped recoverability; it’s triggered under signed agreement amendments (we don’t escrow by default).

Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Security Engineer — Redwood Inference

[attachment: torchservex_attestation_snippet.pdf (stub)]

From: Aimee Harris <aimee.harris@medicore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medicore.com
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: subprocessor roster + provenance artifacts for SIG review

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our GRC reviewer:

1) Can you confirm whether CacheWave’s KV cache encryption keys are customer-specific (i.e., per-customer keys managed by Redwood) or shared across Redwood accounts? If per-customer, who manages the KMS keys and where are they resident?

2) For TorchServeX, can you provide the date of the attestation and the signer (company and role)? Our workflow requires a timestamped attestation within the last 12 months.

If you can answer (1)-(2) and re-send a short one-page summary addressing these two Qs, we can mark the SIG questions as resolved.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — aim is to finish the SIG gating by EOD.

—Aimee

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aimee Harris <aimee.harris@medicore.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: subprocessor roster + provenance artifacts for SIG review

Hi Aimee —

Quick answers below; I’ll also drop a one-page summary to the Drive link Michael included: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-example-shared-evidence

1) CacheWave KMS model: per-customer envelope keys are used. Redwood manages customer-specific data key encryption and the CMKs are in our cloud KMS (AWS us-west-2) by default for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private customers we can integrate with customer-managed KMS via Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK).

2) TorchServeX attestation: signed 2025-03-12 by Clara Nguyen, Head of Trust & Compliance, TorchServeX. The attestation is dated and notarized; I attached the snippet earlier and I’ll include the full attestation PDF in the Drive folder.

Summary (key lines):
- CacheWave: per-customer keys, CMKs in AWS us-west-2 for hosted; BYOK possible.
- TorchServeX attestation: 2025-03-12, signed by Clara Nguyen (Head of Trust & Compliance). No downstream plaintext access.

Let us know if Medicore needs a redacted contract snippet for the escrow clause.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Security Operations — Redwood Inference

[attachment: none; deliverables uploaded to shared Drive]
